resources.string: No completed runtime conclusion is available.
A stable, protocol-confirmed ADB endpoint disagrees with the observed adbd lifecycle. This does not identify a root or hiding implementation.
Debugging settings or runtime activity were observed. ADB can be enabled on an ordinary device and does not establish root access.
Only available sources were evaluated. Permission restrictions, discovery failures and lifecycle transitions limit negative observations.
Debugging restrictions and Test Harness Mode qualify settings; settings and USB gadget state are not hard contradictions against init.
%1$d lifecycle sample(s), %2$d discovery pass(es); latest protocol=%3$s. A contradiction requires the same confirmed listener in repeated passes while init reports stopped.
Settings are context only while policy or Test Harness Mode prevents an ordinary activity interpretation.

An app match does not establish root access, current execution or device compromise. Weak anchors and permission ownership alone do not identify a manager. Missing profiles or signing evidence limit absence conclusions.
Accessible profiles and caller-profile package observations are matched against the manager catalog. Unmatched app identities are excluded from diagnostics.
Signing fingerprints provide catalog identity anchors; unreadable certificates reduce coverage.
Visible payload names provide additional manager anchors; inaccessible directories remain unknown.
Strings from one snapshot are correlated evidence. Names can be spoofed; origin and launch time are unverified. Neither a match nor a negative snapshot establishes current installation or compromise.
A fresh isolated process streams a bounded HPROF snapshot. Binding, dump, timeout and parser failures remain distinguishable in the scan summary.
Exact catalog names are matched in package-name, nice-name and app-data-dir arguments. This app\'s own arguments are excluded; a completed negative snapshot is informational.

Package matches, runtime interfaces and platform behavior checks have separate scopes. Behavior mismatches do not identify a hiding module; timing anomalies have lower confidence. Package history does not establish current installation, and none of these observations proves root access.
A listed probe ran in this scan. Zero hits do not establish full visibility; related package probes can share the same underlying mechanism.
Fixed baseline paths returned EACCES/EPERM. This is a storage visibility indicator and does not identify an installed package or a hiding implementation.
No parent timing sample was collected; this is not a negative detection.

A=invalid type, B=same-length newline prefix; both must return EINVAL. 512 AB/BA pairs, 32 warmups; CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW; paired A−B > 0 ns is positive, 0 ns is baseline, and < 0 ns is negative. Block counts are diagnostic only. Measured in the preload parent without changing CPU affinity. A change from the entry CPU at any sampled endpoint or an incomplete sample invalidates classification. One retained preload is one measurement.
This parent sample supplies the timing verdict.

Pinned child diagnostic (PID=%1$d, CPU=%2$d): paired A−B=%3$s; A=%4$s, B=%5$s; A slower=%6$d/%7$d; blocks positive/negative/zero=%8$d/%9$d/%10$d; CPU migrations=%11$d; collection=%12$s. Child timing is diagnostic only and never replaces the parent sample. Stock A and B already take different kernel paths. Timing direction is supporting information, not proof of hiding, a specific root tool, or a clean environment.
%1$s Collection failed: %2$s. This is not a negative detection. Captured during app_zygote preload; this is a retained measurement, not a live check.
Timing over %1$d pairs: median A=%2$s, B=%3$s, paired A−B=%4$s. The separate App Zygote timing row interprets a validated 512-pair sample; the AVC profile still uses child counts only.

The App Zygote invalid-context A−B paired median was positive. Stock kernels also take different paths for A and B, and CPU/load can change the sign. This is a strong timing anomaly, not proof of KernelSU or root. The AVC counts share the same measurement carrier.
